ideas.description: Equal-time reallocation from the 32 px phase into the 24 px bridge. This is the direct discriminating test between H8.2 (the bridge is worth ~0.13 pp per 1%) and H11 (late full-resolution training is what binds). Base: E100 code (176e5ec). If I116 (low-res Muon lr x1.5) is banked first, rebase onto it and say so in the log. Change only the schedule: 2@16 + 1.75@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 at bs 1024 (was 1.25@24 and 2.75@32). Total samples stay at 7.5 epochs. Resolution switches, LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the renorm cadence and the 32 px-phase Muon factor (1.25x) are indexed by samples, as in E100. The final-EMA window and lookahead stop stay pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes are already static and warmed up in build. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 176e5ec. Pre-registered time: +0.5 epoch at 24 px (~+0.26 s) minus 0.25 epoch at 32 px/bs 1024 (~-0.23 s) gives +0.3 to +0.9%. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes, paired against the pooled E106 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time +0.3 to +0.9% (~4.48-4.51 s). The H8 prediction is a pooled off-seed gain of >= +0.1 pp and a distinct scored mean >= 0.7543. My central estimate is -0.05 to +0.10 pp, because E104 suggests added steps buy about the same anywhere, and this run moves samples rather than adding steps. A gain of >= +0.1 pp at <1% time beats every measured exchange rate. It would become the tip, and its margin would fund a ~1.5% 32 px trim. A result of <= -0.05 pp refutes N8.2 in favour of H11, which closes bridge lengthening.

ideas.description: Class-balanced (stratified) minibatches at zero compute. Base: E100 code. Inside train, at the start of each epoch, build the permutation on the GPU from the global RNG, which the harness seeds per trial. Nothing is built at import or in build. Steps: (1) for each of the 100 classes, shuffle its 500 indices into a [500, 100] (rank, class) index matrix, using one argsort of random keys within class-sorted labels; (2) independently permute the class order within each rank row; (3) flatten row-major. Every consecutive block of 100 then contains each class exactly once, so a bs-1536 batch holds 15-16 images per class and a bs-1024 batch holds 10-11. The class-sorted label index is computed in prepare, which is timed. Samples, steps, shapes and augmentation are unchanged, and the net graph is untouched. Untimed check: the per-batch class-count max-min is <=1 and the epoch covers all 50,000 images exactly once. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes, paired against the E106 pooled baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time within ±0.3%, since a single argsort per epoch costs nothing measurable. Expected accuracy 0 to +0.10 pp. The pass bar is a pooled off-seed gain of >= +0.1 pp with a distinct scored mean >= 0.7543. A pass would make it a free margin source stackable on any tip and funding a ~1.5% 32 px trim. A result within ±0.05 pp closes H12.2. A loss of >= 0.1 pp would mean the batch-to-batch class variance acts as useful noise in this ~280-step regime.

ideas.description: Group-3 width set by tile alignment, decided cheaply first. Step 1, free: read the cuDNN/cutlass kernel names already logged for the group-3 convs at 28/32 px bs 1024 and 24 px bs 1536 (E094/E098/E099/E106 profiler logs). If every group-3 GEMM uses a tile width dividing 576 (64-wide N/M tiles), close H2.19 with no run. Step 2, untimed, only if 128/256-wide tiles appear: in a side script on E100 code, build group-3 widths 512, 576 and 640. Group-3 conv1 input stays 384, the head becomes [100, W], and the Muon stacks are re-batched. Compile and warm up all shapes. Measure ms/step and NVML energy over 20 steps per (resolution, batch) shape, and project total run time over the E100 schedule. Step 3: score 640 on E100 only if it projects <=+1.5% total time. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes against E106, plus two distinct scored samples. If no scored arm is justified, the scored row reruns E100 unchanged as an extra distinct tip sample.
ideas.expected: Most likely outcome: the logs show tile padding on 128-wide tiles (E080: 352/320 recovered only 33-60% of their FLOP savings). Then 640 projects at +0.5 to +1.5% time and 512 at <=-2%, which refutes the 'saves more than FLOP share' half. If 640 is scored, expect +0.05 to +0.15 pp off-seed (capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100: E005, E017), which beats the 0.065 pp per 1% bar when the cost is <=1.5%. If the kernels use 64-wide tiles, H2.19 closes for free.

ideas.description: Multi-sample augmentation in the 32 px phase, at equal compute. Base: E100 code. In the 2.75-epoch 32 px phase only (bs 1024), build each batch from 512 unique images, drawn as the next 512 of the epoch permutation, times 2 augmentation draws. Copy A keeps the existing alternating-flip state and its own translate offsets. Copy B gets the opposite flip and independently drawn translate offsets. Batch shape, step count, LR/EMA/tail indexing and the compiled graphs are unchanged; only the gather indices and the augmentation parameters differ. The 32 px phase then covers ~1.375 unique epochs instead of 2.75. The 16/24/28 px phases are unchanged. Smoke-test that the duplicated indices and the flip parity are correct on one batch. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes against E106, plus one scored sample, and a second only if off-seed >= +0.05 pp.
ideas.expected: Time within ±0.5%. Explore idea with a low-to-moderate prior: Fort et al. report gains on CIFAR-100 at long schedules, but here 32 px exposure appears to bind (E088/E090). Central estimate -0.15 to +0.05 pp off-seed. A pooled gain of >= +0.1 pp would open a whole augmentation-multiplicity axis, including 4 copies and moving it into earlier phases. A result of <= -0.15 pp shows that unique-image coverage dominates at ~7 epochs and closes H12.1.

drop.reason: Low information. It is a tie-breaker projection only, the existing NVML logs lack the per-phase energy for most configs, and I114's untimed profile already records NVML energy for the variants that matter. With E100 robustly banked, no local tie within 3% is pending that would need this.

structured_output.summary:
E106 banked E100 as a robust tip: distinct scored samples average 0.7543, and the pooled off-seed mean is 0.7527 over 3 processes at ~4.46 s. That leaves only ~0.1 pp of local margin. Every measured time trade costs ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1%, so a further cut needs new zero-time accuracy first, or a better exchange rate.

I added four ideas and dropped one.
- **Bridge reallocation (H8.2.1, priority 4):** moves 0.25 epoch of 32 px into the 24 px bridge at roughly equal time. It is the direct discriminating test between the bridge-value hypothesis (H8.2) and late-full-resolution binding (H11), and it is the most likely exploit win.
- **Class-balanced minibatches (H12.2.1, priority 3):** zero compute cost and stackable on any tip.
- **Group-3 width tile alignment (H2.19.1, priority 3):** starts with a free read of the existing kernel-name logs, then an untimed width profile, and is scored only if 640 channels costs ≤1.5% time.
- **Two augmentation copies per image in the 32 px phase (H12.1.1, priority 2):** an explore idea with a low prior.

I dropped I120: it is a tie-break-only analysis, and I114 already captures the NVML energy that matters.

The resulting queue holds 8 ideas: I114, I117, I118, I119 and the four new ones. I116 is still running. Every new idea is decided on ≥3 fresh off-seed processes paired against the pooled E106 baseline, plus distinct scored samples, following the H4 rules.
